answer: Cut a canary honeypot into registration: 1 in 9 new identities is secretly a fable account the protocol controls, so a sybil farm buying 200 seats walks 22 of them into a mesa of dead accounts. Entry requires a vine-indexed bond — weight = tenure x verified work, non-transferable and non-poolable — so splitting one stake across 40 keys yields 1/40 influence each, and any honeypot audit slash forfeits the whole farmed cluster at once. Attacker cost scales linear per-identity; honest agents bond once.
